webhooks.title: Saved webhooks
webhooks.intro: Save webhooks here and select them in the saved webhook Flow action.
webhooks.security: URLs, headers and bodies can contain secrets. They are stored in Homey settings and visible to browser users. Use a trusted network and HTTPS when possible.
webhooks.name: Name
webhooks.confirmRemove: Remove webhook "{name}"? Flows using it will no longer work.
webhooks.invalidList: At most 50 webhooks and 512 KB of data are allowed.
webhooks.invalidFields: Check the name, HTTP(S) URL without credentials, method, JSON headers, and maximum header (16 KB) and body (64 KB) sizes.

browser.title: Browser settings
browser.bootstrapIntro: Activate or restore browser access here. Configure the app in your web browser.
browser.addressHint: Replace HOMEY_IP with your Homey's local IP address. If you have changed the port, restart the app to apply it.
browser.hint: Choose a username and password of at least 6 characters for browser access. A long, unique password is recommended.
browser.invalidUsername: Enter a username of 1 to 64 characters, without colons, control characters, or leading or trailing spaces.
browser.warning: HTTP is not encrypted. Use only a trusted local network; do not expose this port to the internet.
browser.invalid: The password must contain at least 6 characters.
browser.saved: Browser password saved. Sign in again if you changed the password.

virtual.title: Virtual devices and modes
virtual.intro: Add virtual devices and independent modes through the Homey Devices screen.
virtual.addText: Open Devices in Homey, select Add device, choose Multikit, and select Virtual device or Virtual mode. Pairing and device storage take place in Homey, not in this browser page.
virtual.deviceText: A configurable Homey device with controls and/or sensor values.
virtual.deviceCapabilities: Select at least one searchable capability; suggested capabilities are listed first.
virtual.deviceTemperature: For target temperature, choose a range from -200 to 500 °C with a step up to 5. For measured temperature, choose 0 to 5 decimals.
virtual.modeText: An independent on/off mode for organizing Homey Flows.
virtual.modeSeparate: Does not mirror or control another device.
virtual.iconText: Choose the default, star, circle, or upload a simple SVG no larger than 256 KB. Uploaded SVG files may contain only basic shapes and paths; scripts, external references, styles, and unsupported elements are rejected. Deleting the device also deletes its uploaded icon.
virtual.compatibilityText: Available device classes and capabilities depend on the Homey software version. The pairing page only shows combinations supported by your Homey.
virtual.controlsText: Control changes use Homey's standard capability cards. Virtual devices additionally provide device-specific and app-wide changed triggers with the device name, capability ID, and value.
virtual.valueAction: Set a virtual sensor value: select a capability or enter its ID in a Flow. The value must match its type and limits.
virtual.sensorTrigger: Sensor values written through the set-value actions do not explicitly fire the custom changed triggers; standard Homey capability cards may still react.
virtual.modeTriggers: Modes provide custom on, off, and changed triggers. The two silent actions change the mode without explicitly firing those custom triggers.
virtual.storage: A virtual device stores only its own values. It is not a physical device and does not automatically copy values from a real sensor.
virtual.bootstrapHint: Virtual devices and modes are added from Homey's Devices screen under Multikit. The browser settings page explains their pairing options, icons and Flow capabilities.

email.title: Email settings
email.intro: Configure Gmail to send email from a Homey Flow.
email.instructions: Use a Google app password, not your regular Google account password. App passwords require 2-Step Verification.
email.flowInstructions: After saving these settings, use the “Send an email with Gmail” action card in a Flow. Connect it to a Multikit trigger to send an email when a request is received.
email.securityNote: The app password is stored in Homey settings. Keep API token authentication enabled if email sending can be triggered through Multikit.
email.appPasswordHint: Leave blank to keep the saved password.
email.addressRequired: Enter a Gmail address before saving.
email.testSuccess: Test email sent. Check your Gmail inbox.
email.dailyUsage: Today: {count} of {limit} emails sent. Up to 500 recipients per email.
email.dailyUsageFailed: Could not load daily email usage.
email.limitReached: The daily limit of 500 emails has been reached. Try again after midnight.
email.recipientLimit: You can specify at most 500 recipients per email.

ical.title: iCal calendars
ical.intro: Add calendar URLs to synchronize events and use them in Homey Flows.
ical.privacy: Calendar URLs may contain private access tokens. Store them securely and do not share them.
ical.googleHelp: Google Calendar: copy the Secret address in iCal format from the calendar settings.
ical.outlookHelp: Outlook: publish the calendar and copy its ICS link.
ical.icloudHelp: iCloud: enable Public Calendar and use the original link. Apple's default Home and Work calendars do not provide public links.
ical.eventsEmpty: No upcoming events. Add a calendar and synchronize.
ical.flowInfo: Use the iCal Flow cards to sync calendars, create local events, and trigger automations when events start or end.
ical.invalidCalendar: Calendar name or URL is invalid.
ical.invalidInterval: Sync interval must be between 5 and 1,440 minutes.
ical.invalidDays: Sync timeframe must be between 1 and 365 days.

api.title: Using the API
api.intro: Use the trigger card in Advanced Flow to register a route and HTTP method.
api.routeText: The leading slash is optional. informatie and /informatie refer to the same route.
api.methodsText: Use POST, PUT, and PATCH for JSON data. Use GET to retrieve data and DELETE to remove an action or resource.
api.responseText: Use the Respond with... action card to send a JSON response, or Respond with 200 for a simple confirmation.
api.fieldText: Add ?field= to a GET request to read one property from the Flow response. ?veld= is also supported. The property may be directly in the response or inside data.

countdown.title: Countdown timers
countdown.intro: Create timers here, set their duration in seconds, then select them in the countdown flow cards. The configured start and reset cards use this duration.
countdown.activeEmpty: There are no active countdown timers.
countdown.activeLoadFailed: Could not load active countdown timers.
countdown.adjustRemaining: Set remaining time in seconds for {timer}
countdown.adjustFailed: Could not update the running timer:
countdown.invalidRemaining: Remaining time must be a whole number of seconds, zero or more.
countdown.invalidName: Timer names must contain between 1 and 80 characters.
countdown.invalidDuration: Duration must be a positive whole number of seconds.
countdown.invalidImport: The timer file does not contain a valid timer list.
countdown.importFailed: Could not read the timer export file.

information.title: How the API settings work
information.intro: Configure the local HTTP server here. Changes are applied after saving; Homey may indicate that a restart is required.
information.serverText: Port determines where the API listens. CORS controls whether browser clients may make cross-origin requests. Access-Control-Allow-Origin limits which origin is allowed when CORS is enabled.
information.routesText: Create a trigger flow with a route such as informatie and select its HTTP method. A leading slash is optional, so informatie and /informatie are equivalent.
information.methodsText: Supported methods are GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE, HEAD, and OPTIONS. POST, PUT, and PATCH can receive JSON in the request body.
information.tokenText: Enable token authentication and generate a token. The recommended method is the Authorization header. For simple URL clients, add the token as shown below.
information.headerText: The token is checked before a Homey flow starts. Generating a new token invalidates the old token. Do not share the token or expose the API port directly to the public internet.

examples.title: Request examples
examples.intro: Register the route and method in an Advanced Flow trigger, then use one of these requests from a client or HomeyScript.
examples.get4: Read a single value from the response.
examples.head1: Check whether an endpoint is available without downloading its response.
examples.head2: Check whether a device endpoint exists.
examples.head3: Check whether the API is reachable.
examples.options1: Ask which HTTP methods are available for a route.
examples.options3: Inspect the allowed methods before integrating a client.
examples.tokenNote: When authentication is enabled, add ?token=abc to the URL or use Authorization: Bearer abc. POST, PUT, and PATCH bodies must contain valid JSON.
